answer: An auditor would note that identity creation is only expensive if it is metered at the door. Give each inlet a public ledger of ivory tickets: every admission consumes one ticket bound to a live key, and the toll doubles for each extra admission in the same minute, decaying like a willow branch over an hour. A thousand clones admitted in one burst pay exponentially; admitted slowly, they still need a thousand live keys passing ticket checks for weeks. An honest agent buys one ticket at the floor price and never notices the curve.
